text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Some of Australia's biggest companies, including Boral Ltd, BP Australia and AWA, could soon follow in the footsteps of West Australian mining company Valiant Consolidated Ltd, which has launched legal action in the federal court after being denied tax concessions under the federal government's controversial research and development incentive scheme. Companies have told the Senate Economics Legislation Committee's inquiry into amendments to the Industry Research and Development Act that they have been unfairly excluded from claiming tax deductions. Page 1.

Many agree there has been a change of culture at Australia's biggest investor, the AMP Society, since George Turnbull headed up the organisation two years ago but some point to AMP Investments' Andrew Threadgold as the key to AMP's turnaround, with figures showing results in shares, property and bonds have all been average or above average. Page 1.

Major aircraft manufacturer Airbus Industrie has predicted a A$30 billion explosion in orders from the Australasian aviation market in the next 18 years. Airbus said yesterday the region's six biggest carriers, including Qantas, Ansett and Air New Zealand, would between them acquire a further 303 aircraft with 100 seats or more by 2014. Page 7.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Lenfest Communications have thrown further support behind Australis Media Ltd in the form of an estimated US$70 million needed to complete the pay TV operator's US$150 million junk bond issue in the United States. Australis will now be free to go ahead with its satellite pay TV joint venture with Optus Vision and a separate MDS microwave telephony and data partnership with PBL. Page 19.

Despite a slump in net profit from A$7.1 million to A$2.7 million in the year to June 30, Commonwealth Funds Management managing director David Knott says he is still confident the federal government's planned sale of CFM will be completed by the end of the year. Page 19.

The Australian Shareholders Association has confirmed it will seek greater disclosure from Coles Myer Ltd on its commercial settlement on the Yannon transaction and boardroom peace deal at next month's annual meeting. The ASA will also scrutinise related party dealings with executives and directors and the A$2.8 million remuneration package for chief executive Peter Bartels. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an unexpected expansion of BHP's wide-ranging plans to restructure its troubled steel division, the group general manager at BHP Steel's Whyalla operation in South Australia, Noel Cornish, has announced the group plans to cut the Whyalla integrated steel works' 2,400-strong workforce by 10 percent. Page 23.

Prime Television Ltd and fellow regional broadcaster Telecasters Australia Ltd emerged victorious from yesterday's commercial television licence auction and are now set to expand their networks and overcome fierce competition to challenge the monopoly position of the Nine Network affiliates in Mildura and Darwin. Page 23.

Because of a A$190 million bond issue which will allow satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd to complete its US$250 million refinancing, the embattled company will be saddled with an enormous debt burden and will further dilute the interests of long-suffering shareholders. Page 23.

The superannuation industry, led by heavyweight fund managers such as Bankers Trust, Rothschild Australia and Macquarie Bank MBL.AX, is preparing for a full-scale assault on the banking industry's plan retirement savings accounts which are due to be released next year. Page 23.

Tabcorp Holdings Ltd managing director Ross Wilson told shareholders at yesterday's annual meeting in Melbourne he was expecting the group to repeat its strong 1995/96 performance this year, announcing that Tabcorp's revenue for the September quarter had risen about 17 percent. Page 25.

Former New South Wales Premier Neville Wran has described NRMA Ltd president Don Mackay's premature release of the membership's ballot for the group's failed 1994 float just days before the Federal Court ruled that the prospectus was defective as "one of the most arrogant acts of a person in public life in this country". Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Herald understands building products and petroleum group Pioneer International has engaged external consultants for advice on the possible sale of its half-share in Australian Petroleum, Australia's largest petrol refiner, due to serious concerns over its profitability. Page 29.

Telecasters Australia was successful at the Australian Broadcasting Authority's first ever auction of new television licences, paying A$2.1 million for the highly-prized Darwin licence, which will give Telecasters the right to start new stations in Darwin against Kerry Packer's Nine Network . The licence for the Victorian town of Mildura went to Prime Television for A$3.2 million. Page 29.

Utilities Trust of Australia has purchased the federal government-owned investment bank AIDC's 10 percent share in the operator of Sydney's M4 tollway in Parramatta, Statewide Roads, for about A$20 million, saying the New South Wales Government's decision to offer private motorists toll rebates was a contributing factor in the acquisition. Page 29.

A detailed survey of executive remuneration packages paid by Australian companies has revealed the country's chief executives are earning more than ever before, with more than 30 now earning over A$1 million a year, and at least nine earning above A$2 million. Page 29.

Despite a 50 percent fall in net profit from A$400,000 to A$200,000 in the three months to September, due largely to A$5.7 million in abnormal costs associated with pre-opening costs, up from A$3 million, Sydney Harbour Casino is heading into the busy Christmas quarter on a confident note. Page 31.

An AMR Quantum Harris survey of 2,000 people across Australia from November 1995 to February 1996 has revealed new-generation consumers aged 25 and under do not trust themselves with credit cards, a result AQH director Don Porritt says is a clear signal that the free-spending of the 1980s is gone. Page 31.
THE AGE

Although many companies have been actively seeking to cut costs to compensate for the downturn in the economy, the chief executives of Australia's biggest listed companies are being paid record sums, with 30 or more now earning more than A$1 million and at least seven earning A$2 million-plus. Page C1.

Tabcorp chairman Michael Robinson was forced to defend the A$1.3 million 1995/96 salary of managing director Ross Wilson yesterday following a question from a shareholder. Robinson said the 20 percent pay rise was justified in light of the wagering and gaming group's share price doubling in the past year, even though cost-cutting was a stated objective. Page C1.

As part of a 12-month review into the poor performance of its steel division, BHP yesterday announced 250 jobs would be axed from South Australia's Whyalla steelworks. BHP plant chief Neil Cornish said the cuts to the workforce of 2,350 would have a strong impact on the city. Page C1.

Further strong growth in gaming boosted Tabcorp Holdings' first-quarter turnover by 17 percent to A$1.69 billion, managing director Ross Wilson announced yesterday. Wilson predicted Victoria's gambling industry turnover would increase from A$2.57 billion to A$3.04 billion during 1996/97. Page C3.

Following yesterday's auction of the first new free-to-air commercial television licences since 1986, Seven Network affiliate Prime Television won the second commercial broadcast licence in Mildura with a A$3.2 million bid and Ten Network affiliate Telecasters Australia won Darwin's second commercial TV service with a A$2.1 million bid. Page C3.

After Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and U.S. cable TV group Lenfest agreed to purchase a large slice of bonds, investment banks Salomon Brothers and Toronto Dominion threw their support behind Australis Media's US$150 million bond issue, allowing the pay TV group to repay a US$125 million interim loan to Toronto Dominion. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 3873-1800
